operations.comment: ; ActorPositionToWork — physical $6950, CPU $E940, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy actor X's screen coordinate pairs into the work X/Y pairs used by rendering and collision.
; RenderActorFrame — physical $6965, CPU $E955, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Preserve frame A while copying actor coordinates, then enter indexed metasprite rendering.
; RenderIndexedMetasprite — physical $696A, CPU $E95A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; A selects an offset within the resource pointer. Parse signed Y offset, tile, attributes and
; signed X offset records until Y=$80. Reject offscreen pieces and rotate OAM allocation while
; preserving caller X/Y.
; The first resource byte is a relative offset within the graphics resource. Each piece then
; stores dy, tile, attributes, dx; dy=$80 ends the list.
; RenderTwoSpriteFrame — physical $69E1, CPU $E9D1, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; A selects a four-byte tile/attribute pair. Render two adjacent sprites at fixed offsets,
; culling pieces outside the screen; preserve X/Y and advance the rotating OAM cursor.
; Classified data physical [$6A4F,$6A53), CPU [$EA3F,$EA43), PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Two signed Y,X offset pairs for RenderTwoSpriteFrame: (0,0) and (0,8). Y advances
; through all four bytes, including clipped pieces. The preceding negative constant makes
; BMI return to the piece-count check; this table is not the renderer's fallthrough code.
; ApplyCameraDeltaToActor — physical $6A53, CPU $EA43, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Add the signed inverse camera pixel deltas to actor screen coordinates, including high-byte
; carry.
; IntegrateActorVelocity — physical $6A76, CPU $EA66, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Add velocity fractions to position fractions, then signed integer components to screen
; positions with sign extension into the page bytes. Both axes use the same fixed-point
; representation.
; SetActorProposedWorldBounds — physical $6AB5, CPU $EAA5, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Add current camera coordinates to actor X's screen position, retaining the unwrapped camera
; high bytes needed at a world seam.
; SetActorPreviousWorldBounds — physical $6AD6, CPU $EAC6, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Add the previous camera coordinates to actor X's screen position for terrain edge-crossing
; comparisons.
; AimWorkPointAtPlayer — physical $6AF5, CPU $EAE5, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Compute signed player-minus-work deltas, reduce to absolute axes, form a six-bit ratio, and
; look up the angle. Quadrant and major-axis bits restore a full-turn direction in VectorAngle
; while preserving Y.
; Generate six quotient bits from minor/major absolute deltas. Equal axes retain the carry from
; the equality comparison; the next lookup restores the octant.
; SetActorVelocityFromAngle — physical $6B8A, CPU $EB7A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Calculate a signed fixed-point vector from angle/speed and copy it into actor X's velocity
; arrays.
; StoreActorVelocity — physical $6B8D, CPU $EB7D, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy the two work vector pairs into actor X's velocity arrays without recomputing them.
; StoreActorPosition — physical $6BA2, CPU $EB92, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy both work coordinate pairs into actor X's screen position arrays.
; VectorFromAnglePixels — physical $6BB7, CPU $EBA7, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Calculate a signed integer vector using the angle and radius. This entry leaves the high byte
; zero before applying the sign.
; VectorFromAngleFixed — physical $6BBB, CPU $EBAB, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Calculate a signed vector scaled by sixteen for fixed-point velocity. Fold angles into a
; quarter-wave lookup, multiply by the magnitude, scale and restore the original sign.
; VectorComponentFromPhase — physical $6BD3, CPU $EBC3, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Compute one signed component, with the selected integer/fixed scale. A is the component phase;
; the shared wrapper computes the quarter-turn component first.
; Fixed mode shifts the product left four before sign restoration. Integer mode stores an
; unsigned magnitude with zero high byte first.
; Classified data physical [$6C30,$6C50), CPU [$EC20,$EC40).
; 32 per-slot phase values used to stagger random firing attempts across a 32-frame cycle.
; TryRandomActorShot — physical $6C50, CPU $EC40, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; On a slot-staggered 32-frame schedule, compare a random byte with probability A. On success
; enter aimed enemy-bullet creation.
; TryAimedActorShot — physical $6C62, CPU $EC52, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Only visible actors may shoot. Aim toward the player and enter the minimum-distance/allocation
; checks.
; TryActorShotWithCurrentAngle — physical $6C6E, CPU $EC5E, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Only visible actors may shoot; retain the already selected angle and deltas for the shared
; distance/allocation checks.
; CreateEnemyBulletIfDistant — physical $6C74, CPU $EC64, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Reject shots too close to the player on both axes. Find a free bullet slot, calculate
; difficulty-dependent fixed velocity and initialize its screen position and fractions.
; TurnActorTowardPlayerWithJitter — physical $6CCA, CPU $ECBA, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Set the jitter option and enter bounded turning toward the player.
; TurnActorTowardPlayer — physical $6CCE, CPU $ECBE, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Move the actor's angle toward the player's direction by signed step A. Optional jitter perturbs
; the final angle; then recompute velocity at the existing speed.
; CullActorOutsideScreen — physical $6D0F, CPU $ECFF, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Check the coordinate page bytes and hitbox allowances against screen bounds. Free an outlying
; actor and return carry; retain it and return clear otherwise.
; CopyVelocityToNextActor — physical $6D42, CPU $ED32, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy both velocity axes and heading from actor X to its following slot. The chain caller
; supplies a valid neighbor.
; UpdateEnemyBullets — physical $6D61, CPU $ED51, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Integrate bullet fixed-point motion, cull at margins, optionally add camera motion in the
; vehicle stage, and test terrain/player collision. Surviving bullets draw one animated OAM
; sprite.
; UpdateActors — physical $403F, CPU $C02F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Visit all 32 actor slots backwards. Active nonnegative types select a handler and graphics
; resource from parallel 24-entry pointer tables; negative nonempty types play a timed
; destruction animation, then free the slot and may create a pickup.
; The two 24-entry directories are parallel: type selects both code and its default graphics
; resource.
; UpdateDestroyedActor — physical $4073, CPU $C063, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Animate a destroyed actor for 16 updates. Certain types choose deterministic drops; others use
; a bounded random drop. Copy the old position into an available pickup slot before releasing the
; actor.
; The empty-slot test returns a negative type on success. Failure simply suppresses the drop, not
; actor cleanup.
; FindFreePickupSlot — physical $40D4, CPU $C0C4, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Search the 16 pickup slots backwards. A negative type denotes an unused slot; return Y and the
; negative flag, or nonnegative A when full.
; UpdateGraduallyTurningActor — physical $40E1, CPU $C0D1, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Periodically recompute a coarse target heading, attempt a shot, and change the heading by one
; step every eight staggered frames. Render the selected heading and apply collision/offscreen
; handling.
; UpdateSineFlyingActor — physical $414A, CPU $C13A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Integrate horizontal fixed-point velocity while deriving vertical position from a mirrored
; waveform. Type and movement sign select the animation variant; remove actors beyond their
; permitted horizontal edge.
; UpdateSegmentedTrailActor — physical $41E8, CPU $C1D8, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Build five successive rendered/collidable segments along a direction vector. Stage mode
; controls acceleration; remove the actor beyond the expanded viewport and advance its direction
; otherwise.
; UpdateEightPartController — physical $4291, CPU $C281, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Animate the controller and periodically fire. The central instance alternates between launching
; its eight referenced parts and assigning them trajectories around the player. The shared part
; count gates the next launch. A synthetic center-X=$80 activation probe launched the reserved
; parts, corroborating this state transition without establishing a natural encounter or defeat.
; LaunchEightControllerParts — physical $4317, CPU $C307, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Reset all eight referenced actor slots, assign table-driven vertical positions, horizontal
; speeds and delays, and fan their vertical velocities by half-group.
; The eight saved slot indices are a stage-local array, not pointers to ROM records.
; Classified data physical [$4363,$436B), CPU [$C353,$C35B).
; Eight initial Y coordinates for the eight-part controller launch.
; Classified data physical [$436B,$4373), CPU [$C35B,$C363).
; Eight initial horizontal velocity low bytes; the constructor doubles the signed pair before
; use.
; Classified data physical [$4373,$437B), CPU [$C363,$C36B).
; Eight launch delays. The following terminated sequence selects the controller's animation
; frames.
; Classified data physical [$437B,$438A), CPU [$C36B,$C37A).
; Controller animation sequence; a negative byte resets the cursor to zero.
; DelayPartReactivation — physical $438A, CPU $C37A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Every fourth frame decrement the part delay. On expiry clear its inactive phase and install the
; next long delay.
; UpdateControllerPart — physical $43A0, CPU $C390, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Handle dormant, delayed and moving part phases, then animate, collide and cull. Expiration or
; leaving the viewport decrements the controller's active-part count once and leaves a dormant
; part record.
; UpdateDirectionAnimatedActor — physical $43F9, CPU $C3E9, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Integrate velocity and choose graphics from state and coarse heading, then perform collision
; checks. This handler intentionally shares the common rendering/collision helpers.
; RecoilChargingActor — physical $442A, CPU $C41A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Apply an eight-step signed horizontal recoil table; after the last step clear the recoil bit
; and arm the longer idle delay.
; UpdateChargingActor — physical $445F, CPU $C44F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Track the player's Y position with fractional steps, then charge horizontally. Hitting an edge
; or solid terrain returns to an idle/recoil phase. Animate by facing and frame parity and
; perform the common collision test.
; Classified data physical [$4557,$455F), CPU [$C547,$C54F).
; Eight signed horizontal recoil steps. Actor facing reverses their sign.
; UpdateFlashingActor — physical $455F, CPU $C54F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Apply camera displacement, render one of four phase-staggered frames (with a stage-specific
; variant), and perform a probabilistic shot attempt and collision test.
; UpdateAcceleratingActor — physical $4585, CPU $C575, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Use a fixed stage-specific horizontal speed or accelerate its signed velocity over time.
; Integrate, animate, collide and cull, then attempt a shot with the handler's probability bound.
; UpdateBouncingActor — physical $45E1, CPU $C5D1, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Add vertical gravity, integrate both axes, and resolve terrain. Reverse X velocity at a side
; collision; at a lower collision derive rebound strength from vertical distance to the player,
; then reverse Y. Select animation by X direction.
; UpdateDelayedReversingActor — physical $4661, CPU $C651, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Wait, enter a spinning phase, then reverse and double both velocity components. Its timer
; separates the phases; common rendering, collision and offscreen removal follow.
; UpdateDroppingActor — physical $46BD, CPU $C6AD, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Wait until horizontally close to the player, then descend two pixels per update. Camera
; displacement and the left-side removal rule apply before animation/collision.
; UpdateOrbitingEmitter — physical $4700, CPU $C6F0, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Periodically reduce its lifetime counter and turn toward the player. On expiry become a
; destruction-state actor. Draw the emitter and three satellites from signed direction vectors;
; phase bits and random checks vary their rotation.
; RenderOrbitSatellite — physical $47E3, CPU $C7D3, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Render a small satellite at the work point using the frame animation, then run its collision
; test without replacing the parent actor coordinates.
; UpdateVerticalLungeActor — physical $47F3, CPU $C7E3, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Alternate a 30-frame lunge toward the player's Y position with a 40-frame rest. During the
; active phase integrate velocity; animate the phase, collide, cull and attempt shots.
; UpdateDelayedDriftingActor — physical $484A, CPU $C83A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; During its initial timer move left one pixel each frame, then use normal fixed-point motion.
; Render its fixed frame and apply collision/offscreen removal.
; UpdateExpandingRingActor — physical $4873, CPU $C863, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Move and fire periodically, then vary a ring radius through expansion, contraction and a timed
; pause. Render eight equally spaced satellites around an offset center; the radius and angular
; phase live in shared stage scratch.
; UpdateGravityActorVariant — physical $4949, CPU $C939, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Choose a stage-specific graphics resource and hitbox, apply gravity, then integrate and resolve
; terrain. A timer changes the vertical velocity from its parameter; collisions reverse X or stop
; Y before rendering.
; UpdateThresholdHomingActor — physical $49EA, CPU $C9DA, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; After its delay, move until the screen Y reaches a stored threshold. Aim at the player once,
; install velocity and a new delay, then animate by coarse heading and use common
; collision/culling/shooting.
; UpdateScriptedPathActor — physical $4A48, CPU $CA38, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Read direction and doubled duration from a path stream selected by state. A set duration high
; bit supplies a new speed byte. Preserve the stream cursor in the actor and update its velocity
; when a new record is read.
; Path durations are shifted left: bit 7 is an optional speed operand flag, with the remaining
; bits becoming a doubled timer.
; UpdateLinearActor — physical $4AAF, CPU $CA9F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Integrate velocity and camera displacement, select animation from coarse direction, then
; collide and remove outside the viewport.
; UpdateRisingShooter — physical $4ACC, CPU $CABC, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Move upward two pixels per update, render its state frame, and occasionally fire on a slot-
; staggered random schedule.
; UpdateThreePartChain — physical $4AFB, CPU $CAEB, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; The leader periodically propagates velocity to its two following slots, fires and eventually
; frees all three slots. Each member moves; only the leader renders and tests the shared hitbox.
; UpdateWanderingShooter — physical $4B56, CPU $CB46, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; At each firing interval perturb the heading by a signed random offset, turn toward the player,
; and then move/render/collide through the common helpers.
; AdvanceCameraAndQueueEdges — physical $37FF, CPU $B7EF, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Save the previous camera and PPU scroll state, then add signed pixel deltas. World high bytes
; wrap at the stage dimensions; vertical PPU scroll wraps at 240 pixels and changes the nametable
; bit. Only a crossed 8-pixel boundary queues fresh tiles and attribute nibbles. Finish by
; committing scroll and negating deltas for screen-relative objects.
; X is the sign extension of the signed pixel step; retain the unwrapped high byte for seam-aware
; collision probes.
; Wrap the world coordinate by stage height, independently of the 240-pixel PPU scroll cycle
; below.
; For upward underflow the carry convention requires subtracting 10 rather than F0; the result is
; the wrapped 0..239 scroll value.
; CommitCameraScroll — physical $38AD, CPU $B89D, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Negate each camera delta into its signed screen displacement, commit the staged PPU scroll, and
; release the staging counter. Shared by the no-edge and completed-edge paths.
; These cells change meaning at commit: camera motion becomes inverse screen displacement for
; actors and pickups.
; QueueHorizontalScrollEdge — physical $38D3, CPU $B8C3, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Choose the entering tile column from movement sign. Split its 30 tile writes across vertical
; nametables, fetch metatiles, and pack the affected attribute quadrants. The extra lookahead
; bytes handle partial tiles at the viewport edge.
; Four shifts splice adjacent metatile attribute nibbles when the viewport does not begin on the
; matching attribute boundary.
; AppendColumnAttributePatch — physical $3A34, CPU $BA24, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Append one masked attribute value plus its PPU address to the column patch arrays. The IRQ
; later merges the preserved quadrants with VRAM.
; QueueVerticalScrollEdge — physical $3A48, CPU $BA38, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Choose the entering row from vertical movement, wrap its tile coordinate at 30 rows, fetch 37
; tiles and rotate the first 32 into the row buffer. Queue attribute half-byte patches only on
; even tile rows, including the horizontal seam.
; The first and last partial attribute quadrants meet across the horizontal nametable seam.
; AppendRowAttributePatch — physical $3BA6, CPU $BB96, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Append a masked attribute patch and advance within its eight-byte attribute row. Wrap the low
; three address bits without advancing into the next row.
; LocateStageMetatile — physical $3BCB, CPU $BBBB, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Convert tile coordinates to a wrapped stage screen index. Read its little-endian layout
; pointer, then return Y as the 8 by 8 metatile index and local tile coordinates in the work
; bytes.
; The screen directory is row-major: (row * stage_width + column) * 2.
; CameraToTileCoordinates — physical $3C47, CPU $BC37, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy the current camera world coordinates into the work pair, then divide both unsigned 16-bit
; axes by eight.
; WorldToTileCoordinates — physical $3C57, CPU $BC47, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Divide both work coordinate pairs by eight in place; the high bytes remain part of the shift.
; ResolvePlayerTerrain — physical $3C72, CPU $BC62, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Probe the moved player's terrain edges. Apply the resolved screen position on blocked axes and
; mark death for terrain at or above the lethal threshold.
; ResolveActorTerrain — physical $3C9F, CPU $BC8F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Probe actor X's previous and proposed world bounds; on a blocked axis replace its screen
; coordinate pair with the returned corrected position.
; ProbeMovedTerrainEdges — physical $3CBF, CPU $BCAF, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Compare old/new world positions independently on X and Y. Only newly crossed 8-pixel boundaries
; need a terrain scan. Return blocked-axis bits in TerrainFlags and camera-relative corrected
; coordinates; X is preserved by the scan helpers.
; ScanHorizontalTerrainEdge — physical $3D56, CPU $BD46, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Select the left or right edge from movement sign, expand a vertical tile strip, and search its
; terrain classes backwards. Carry reports a class at or above SolidTileThreshold; the maximum
; encountered blocking class is retained for the caller.
; The extra three output positions cover unaligned partial tiles; only the requested probe span
; is tested for blocking.
; ScanVerticalTerrainEdge — physical $3DA6, CPU $BD96, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Select the upper or lower edge, expand a horizontal tile strip, and search backwards for a
; terrain class meeting SolidTileThreshold. Return carry and the blocking class.
; ApplyStageDistortionToProbe — physical $3DF6, CPU $BDE6, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; In the distorted stage, adjust the work X position using its scanline band before looking up
; terrain. Other stages leave the coordinates untouched.
; ExpandVerticalTileStrip — physical $3E00, CPU $BDF0, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; A is the tile-buffer end index. Locate the starting screen/metatile, expand four vertically
; adjacent tiles per metatile, and walk stage screens when the local Y index wraps. Large
; requests also collect one terrain/attribute class per metatile.
; Requests of sixteen or more use the graphics buffer and append class bytes; shorter requests
; fill the probe buffer directly.
; ExpandHorizontalTileStrip — physical $3ED0, CPU $BEC0, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; A is the tile-buffer end index. Expand each metatile's four horizontal tiles and advance to the
; next screen at an eight-metatile row boundary. Large requests produce both graphics and the
; terrain/attribute class buffer.
; Eight metatiles span a screen row. Crossing that boundary fetches the neighboring screen
; pointer, including stage wrap.
; TestSolidWorldPoint — physical $3F96, CPU $BF86, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Look up the terrain class at the work world point and compare it with the solid threshold.
; Carry reports a blocking class.
; TestBulletWorldPoint — physical $3F9C, CPU $BF8C, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Return carry only for a terrain class in the half-open solid-to-lethal threshold range. Higher
; classes do not stop these bullets.
; ReadWorldTerrainClass — physical $3FA8, CPU $BF98, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Convert the work world point to a stage metatile and local 4 by 4 tile index, then read the
; selected tile class. Preserve actor X. Shared lookup for player bullets and enemy bullets.
; Classified data physical [$3FDF,$400F), CPU [$BFCF,$BFFF).
; 24 little-endian actor handler pointers. UpdateActors indexes by nonnegative actor type;
; negative nonempty values are destruction states, FF is empty.
; Classified data physical [$400F,$403F), CPU [$BFFF,$C02F).
; 24 parallel little-endian graphics-resource pointers for the actor handlers. Handler-internal
; variants may replace the selected resource.
; CHR ROM physical [$8010,$10010): four physical 8 KiB pattern banks, NES two-bitplane tiles.
; CHR also carries CPU-uploaded resources/code: LoadChrResourceToRam reads through PPUDATA.
; Image classification describes storage; it does not imply every tile is displayed graphics.
; Exact uploaded routine origins/schemas remain local questions; no extracted assets are shared.
; LoadChrResourceToRam source segments, physical offsets including the iNES header:
; 8: $FEED +291, $D010 +733; 9: $D2E8 +296, then 728 non-CHR bytes.
; These are loader read origins under its CHR page selection, not a code/data split inside
; Image storage. Only resource 9 crosses into PPU nametable space at $2000.
; TestActorCollisions — physical $6582, CPU $E572, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Ignore work points outside the visible world page. Check player and satellite rectangles, then
; all player shots. Shot kind selects point or extended beam geometry; successful hits dispatch
; by collision class through nine handler pointers.
; The collision class is supplied by each actor handler. Dispatch retains the shot index in Y and
; actor index in X through the saved work slot.
; TestHorizontalBeamCollision — physical $6642, CPU $E632, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Compare the target rectangle with a horizontal beam whose length extends its X range, then
; rejoin the shared hit dispatch.
; TestVerticalBeamCollision — physical $6663, CPU $E653, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Use beam length on the Y axis and the ordinary target X range. Failed geometry advances to the
; next shot.
; TestDiagonalBeamCollision — physical $6684, CPU $E674, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Use three-quarters of beam age as extent, reject outside the expanded rectangle, then test
; diagonal overlap against the target's shorter dimension. Success enters the shared collision
; dispatch.
; NormalizeBeamCollisionQuadrant — physical $66F5, CPU $E6E5, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Copy shot and target coordinates to scratch, mirror selected quadrants around zero and adjust
; rectangle origins, then select horizontal, vertical or diagonal collision geometry from
; direction bits.
; Classified data physical [$6758,$676A), CPU [$E748,$E75A).
; Nine little-endian collision handler pointers selected by CollisionClassOrSpawnType during
; actor collision. These implement ordinary destruction, health and special stage/controller
; contracts.
; DamageActorFromSatellite — physical $676A, CPU $E75A, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Set the satellite-damage entry flag before the common susceptibility test; one additional type
; is immune to satellite hits.
; DamageActorFromBomb — physical $676D, CPU $E75D, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Clear the satellite flag and enter the common susceptibility test. Several controller/special
; types are immune; susceptible actors receive score and become negative destruction states.
; AbsorbShotWithImpact — physical $67AF, CPU $E79F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Play the impact sound, start a short player-shot hit animation, and restore the caller's actor
; index before returning from collision processing.
; DestroyActorFromShot — physical $67BC, CPU $E7AC, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Award the type-dependent score, enter actor destruction, and consume ordinary shots. Beam shots
; persist through the hit.
; DamageActorHealth — physical $67F1, CPU $E7E1, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Subtract the shot-kind damage count; zero or underflow destroys the actor, otherwise absorb the
; hit with an impact animation.
; HitControllerPart — physical $6800, CPU $E7F0, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Dormant FF-state parts ignore hits. An active part receives a recovery timer and absorbs the
; shot.
; HitEightPartController — physical $6812, CPU $E802, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Choose damage from hit position, then damage the central controller. On defeat clear its mode,
; destroy all eight part slots and enter the common destruction path.
; HitStageTarget — physical $6857, CPU $E847, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Flash the stage palette and damage the target. A defeated target decrements the remaining
; count, possibly sets stage clear and awards a stage-specific score, then destroys the actor.
; HitArenaMarker — physical $6877, CPU $E867, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Update the remaining target count/clear state, mark the marker consumed and create a
; destruction actor at the work position. Consume the impacting shot.
; HitFinalStageTarget — physical $68C0, CPU $E8B0, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Flash the palette and apply damage; defeat sets stage clear while keeping this handler's
; distinct collision-return path.
; HitChainSegment — physical $68D3, CPU $E8C3, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Only specific segment states are vulnerable. Hits either propagate a neighboring state or
; reopen adjacent nodes with difficulty-based health before destroying this segment; other states
; absorb the impact.
; SubtractSpecialTargetHealth — physical $6911, CPU $E901, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Scale requested damage for the shot kind and subtract it. A surviving target discards this
; helper's return address and transfers directly to impact handling; underflow returns to the
; caller's defeat path. Exact zero is still a surviving result here.
; The special target helper returns only after borrow. A nonborrow result, including exact zero,
; removes its own return address and ends the collision via the impact path.
; ReverseActorXVelocity — physical $692C, CPU $E91C, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Negate the full signed 16-bit horizontal velocity, including fractional carry.
; ReverseActorYVelocity — physical $693E, CPU $E92E, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Negate the full signed 16-bit vertical velocity.
; ROMAtlas NES commentary source; ROM-derived source/assets remain local.
; Physical offsets include the 16-byte iNES header. PRG CPU view is [0,1,2,3].
; Static structure and observed execution provenance remain in baseline.json/review.json.
; RunTitleAttractAndGame — physical $6E40, CPU $EE30, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; Run the title/options RAM helper. Idle selection cycles three recorded attract stages; player
; selection initializes new game or password state, then runs stages and the continue/menu helper
; until returning to title.
; StartGameStage — physical $6E9F, CPU $EE8F, PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
